# CLAUDE.md

How Claude works in this project. This file is the **rulebook**: it rarely changes.
Facts about the project (goals, plan, progress) live in the memory file below.

**Do not edit this file unless the user asks.**

## Project memory
@.claude/memory/PROJECT.md

The line above loads `.claude/memory/PROJECT.md` into every session. It holds the
project's overview, goals, requirements, tech stack, commands, plan and progress.
- Read it first. Treat it as the source of truth for what we're building and where we are.
- If it still has `TODO`s, help the user fill them in before starting work.

## Folder structure
- `src/` — main code.
- `tests/` — automated tests; mirror the layout of `src/`.
- `docs/` — longer documentation: guides, design notes, decisions.
- `scripts/` — developer helper scripts (setup, build, release). Not app code.
- `.claude/` — Claude Code settings and memory.

Put new files in the folder that matches. If none fits, ask before creating a new top-level folder.

## Conventions
- Follow the existing style of the file you are editing.
- Keep changes small and focused on the task; don't refactor unrelated code.
- Add or update tests alongside code changes.
- Never commit secrets. Configuration that varies per machine goes in `.env`
  (git-ignored); document required variables in `.env.example`.

## Before finishing a task
1. Run the test and lint commands from `PROJECT.md` and make sure they pass.
2. Update docs (README, `docs/`) if behaviour, commands, or structure changed.

## Wrapping up a session
When the user runs `/wrap-up` or says "wrap up", follow the `wrap-up` skill
(`.claude/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md`). It updates `.claude/memory/PROJECT.md`.
